BUS.G11.T4.HR.A1.title: Introduction to Human Resources
BUS.G11.T4.HR.A1.description: An introduction to the human resources function: recruitment, selection and interviewing; the legalities of employment contracts; induction and placement; salary determination (piecemeal and time-related, including personal tax); and employee benefits. Relevant Acts: LRA, BCEA, EEA, COIDA.
BUS.G11.T4.HR.A1.strand: T4 — Team dynamics, conflict & Human Resources
BUS.G11.T4.HR.A1.recovery_strategy: Recruitment = attracting applicants; selection = choosing the best; induction = settling the new employee in. BCEA sets basic conditions, EEA promotes equity, LRA governs labour relations, COIDA covers workplace injuries.

questions.question: _________ means attracting suitable applicants to apply for a job.
questions.memo: Recruitment is the process of attracting suitable people to apply for a vacant post, for example by advertising it.

questions.question: What does selection involve?
options: Choosing the best candidate from the applicants
questions.expected: Choosing the best candidate from the applicants
questions.memo: Selection is choosing the most suitable applicant, using tools like screening and interviews.

questions.question: True or false: An employment contract sets out the terms agreed between employer and employee.
questions.memo: An employment contract is a legal agreement stating the duties, pay and conditions agreed between employer and employee.

questions.question: _________ helps a new employee settle into the job and the workplace.
questions.memo: Induction introduces a new employee to the workplace, the team and their role so they can settle in.

questions.question: Which Act sets the basic conditions of employment, such as working hours and leave?
options: The Basic Conditions of Employment Act (BCEA)
questions.expected: The Basic Conditions of Employment Act (BCEA)
questions.memo: The BCEA sets minimum employment conditions such as working hours, leave and notice periods.

questions.question: True or false: A pension is an example of an employee benefit.
questions.memo: Benefits such as a pension, medical aid and leave are rewards beyond the basic salary.

questions.question: Put the steps of hiring a new employee in the correct order.

items.text: Advertise the post to attract applicants
Appoint and induct the chosen person

questions.memo: Recruitment then selection: advertise, shortlist, interview, then appoint and induct the chosen candidate.

questions.question: Sort each task into recruitment, selection or induction.

items.text: Showing a new hire around the workplace
Posting the vacancy on a job site
Checking references and choosing the best applicant
Explaining the new employee's duties on day one

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Recruitment attracts applicants (adverts); selection chooses the best (interviews, references); induction settles them in (orientation).

questions.question: What is the difference between time-related and piecemeal salary determination?
options: Time-related pays for time worked; piecemeal pays per unit produced
Time-related pays per unit; piecemeal pays per hour
questions.expected: Time-related pays for time worked; piecemeal pays per unit produced
questions.memo: Time-related pay is based on hours or a monthly period; piecemeal pay is based on the number of items produced.

questions.question: _________ pay is calculated according to the number of units a worker produces.
questions.memo: Piecemeal (piece-rate) pay rewards output — the more units produced, the higher the pay.

questions.question: Which Act promotes equity and protects employees from unfair discrimination at work?
questions.memo: The Employment Equity Act promotes fair treatment and equal opportunity, prohibiting unfair discrimination in the workplace.

questions.question: True or false: COIDA covers compensation for employees injured or made ill at work.
questions.memo: The Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA) compensates workers injured or made ill on the job.

questions.question: Sort each Act under what it mainly deals with.

items.text: Rules on working hours and leave
Paying out for a workplace injury

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: BCEA = basic conditions (hours, leave); EEA = equity and fair treatment; COIDA = compensation for workplace injury.

questions.question: Which of these are examples of employee benefits?
questions.memo: Benefits are rewards beyond the basic salary, such as pension contributions and medical aid.

questions.question: What does induction of a new employee involve?
options: Introducing them to the workplace, the team and their role
questions.expected: Introducing them to the workplace, the team and their role
questions.memo: Induction helps a new hire settle in by introducing the workplace, colleagues and their responsibilities.

questions.question: A legal agreement that sets out an employee's duties, pay and conditions is an _________ contract.
questions.memo: An employment contract is the legal agreement governing the relationship between employer and employee.

questions.question: An employee is unfairly dismissed and believes labour rights were ignored. Which Act mainly governs this dispute?
questions.memo: The Labour Relations Act governs fair labour practices, including unfair dismissals and disputes between employers and employees.

questions.question: Why should a business follow proper recruitment and selection procedures?
options: To choose the best candidate fairly and comply with the law
To make hiring as slow as possible
To avoid ever filling the post
questions.expected: To choose the best candidate fairly and comply with the law
questions.memo: Proper procedures help find the most suitable person fairly and keep the business within labour law, avoiding disputes.

questions.question: A factory pays workers for each garment they sew, while the office pays staff a fixed monthly salary. How are these pay methods best described?
options: The factory uses piecemeal pay; the office uses time-related pay
The factory uses time-related pay; the office uses piecemeal pay
Neither is a real pay method
questions.expected: The factory uses piecemeal pay; the office uses time-related pay
questions.memo: Paying per garment is piecemeal (per unit); a fixed monthly salary is time-related (per period).

questions.question: Why must an employer understand the relevant labour Acts when employing staff?
options: To meet legal duties on conditions, equity, safety and injury compensation, avoiding penalties
Because the Acts have no effect on business
To avoid ever paying any salary
questions.expected: To meet legal duties on conditions, equity, safety and injury compensation, avoiding penalties
questions.memo: The BCEA, EEA, LRA and COIDA place legal duties on employers; understanding them keeps the business compliant and protects both staff and the business.
